problems.title: A radical logarithmic substitution
problems.question: Solve2(log₂x)²+20=20log₂x+5√[(log₂x)²−5log₂(x²)+16].
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Set t=log₂x,x>0. The radicand is t²−10t+16. Let u=√(t²−10t+16)≥0.
steps: The equation becomes2u²−12=5u,or(2u+3)(u−4)=0. Thus u=4.
Then t²−10t+16=16,so t=0 or10.
Both give valid original roots.

problems.title: Derivative of a nested inverse-trigonometric power
problems.question: Differentiate $f(x)=3^{\ln\sqrt{\arcsin\sqrt{2-x^2}}}$.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: Apply the power and chain rules:f′=(ln3/2)u^(ln3/2−1)u′.
The original domain is(−√2,−1]∪[1,√2); the derivative formula applies where1<x²<2.

problems.title: All tangents cutting an axis triangle of area20
problems.question: Find lines tangent to y=x²+5 whose intercept triangle with the coordinate axes has area20.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: At contact abscissa t,the tangent is y=2tx+5−t². For t≠0,area=(5−t²)²/(4|t|).
steps: Let u=|t|>0. The area condition is(u²−5)²=80u,or(u−5)(u³+5u²+15u−5)=0.
The cubic factor is strictly increasing on u>0 and has one positive root u₀≈0.301258383.
Thus t=±5 or±u₀. Each produces a distinct valid intercept triangle.
problems.answer: y=±10x−20 and y=±2u₀x+5−u₀²,where u₀ is the unique positive root of u³+5u²+15u−5=0.

problems.title: Graph a rational function
problems.question: Sketch f(x)=(x²+2)/(3x).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The graph is odd,has vertical asymptote x=0 and oblique asymptote y=x/3,and crosses neither axis.
It increases for|x|>√2 and decreases for0<|x|<√2.
It has local maximum(−√2,−2√2/3) and local minimum(√2,2√2/3).
It is concave down for x<0 and concave up for x>0; range is(−∞,−2√2/3]∪[2√2/3,∞).
problems.answer: Use the two branches and labeled asymptotes described above.

problems.title: A two-sided limit with opposite infinite exponents
problems.question: Find lim as x→π/3 of[(1−sin2x)/(1+cos^(5/2)x)]^tan(x+π/6).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: As x approachesπ/3 from the left,the exponent tends to+∞,so the expression tends to0.
From the right,it tends to−∞,so the expression tends to+∞.
problems.answer: The two-sided limit does not exist; left limit0,right limit+∞.

problems.title: Shade a trigonometric region
problems.question: Describe and shade points(x,y)∈(0,3)² with cos²(x+y)≤cos²(x−y).
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The inequality requires sin2x sin2y≥0. On(0,3),sin2x is positive belowπ/2 and negative aboveπ/2.
Thus shade the lower-left square0<x,y≤π/2 and the upper-right squareπ/2≤x,y<3.
Include all points of the internal lines x=π/2 or y=π/2; exclude the outer boundary x,y=0,3.
problems.answer: The two same-sign squares plus the internal equality lines.

problems.title: An ellipse rectangle determined by normals
problems.question: An ellipse is x²/49+y²/24=1. Normals at the vertices of an inscribed rectangle divide the focal segment in ratio3:4. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Foci are(±5,0). A normal at(x,y) meets the x-axis at x−24x/49=25x/49.
steps: Dividing[−5,5] in ratio3:4 gives axis coordinates±5/7. Thus rectangle vertex abscissas are±7/5.
Substitute to obtain y²=24(1−1/25)=576/25,so y=±24/5.
Width=14/5,height=48/5; perimeter=2(62/5).

problems.title: Height between parallel parabola chords
problems.question: A trapezoid is inscribed in y=x². Its bases make60° with the y-axis,and their midpoint distance is2. Find its height.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For a chord y=mx+b,the endpoint x-coordinates sum to m,so its midpoint has x=m/2.
steps: The base midpoints therefore lie on a vertical line,with vertical separation2.
A base makes30° with the horizontal,so the perpendicular separation is2cos30°.

problems.title: Opposite-edge sums in an orthocentric tetrahedron
problems.question: All four altitudes of tetrahedron ABCD are concurrent,and AB=CD=1. Find the sum of squares of all six edges.
problems.idea: Apply the formulas below and keep track of domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: In an orthocentric tetrahedron,opposite edges are perpendicular and AB²+CD²=AC²+BD²=AD²+BC².
steps: The shared pair sum is1+1=2.
There are three such pairs,so the total is3·2.
